sub_topic.description: 13-year academic progression (K-12) for Religious Wars and Counter-Reformation in The Renaissance & The Reformation (Roots of Individual Conscience) (History & Social Studies)

objectives.topic_name: The Renaissance & The Reformation (Roots of Individual Conscience)
objectives.objective_text: Describe how the Catholic Church responded to the Reformation through the Council of Trent and new religious orders like the Jesuits.

objectives.topic_name: The Renaissance & The Reformation (Roots of Individual Conscience)
objectives.objective_text: Explain the multiple causes and effects of the religious wars that divided Europe after the Reformation.

standards: C3 D2.His.14.6-8 — Explain multiple causes and effects of events and developments in the past (history, grades 6-8)

objectives.topic_name: The Renaissance & The Reformation (Roots of Individual Conscience)
objectives.objective_text: Analyze how the Counter-Reformation connected to broader political and religious developments in 16th- and 17th-century Europe.

standards: C3 D2.His.1.6-8 — Analyze connections among events and developments in broader historical contexts (history, grades 6-8)

objectives.topic_name: The Renaissance & The Reformation (Roots of Individual Conscience)
objectives.objective_text: Analyze the causes and consequences of the Thirty Years' War and its resolution in the Peace of Westphalia in 1648.

standards: C3 D2.His.14.9-12 — Analyze multiple and complex causes and effects of events in the past (history, grades 9-12)

objectives.topic_name: The Renaissance & The Reformation (Roots of Individual Conscience)
objectives.objective_text: Evaluate how the religious wars and Counter-Reformation were shaped by a divided Europe and assess their broader impact on the modern state system and religious toleration.

standards: C3 D2.His.1.9-12 — Evaluate how historical events and developments were shaped by unique circumstances of time and plac (history, grades 9-12)
